subject: Mathematics
source: Original supplementary learning draft aligned to Class 6 Ganita Prakash Chapter 5 (fegp105.pdf), Reprint 2026–27. Verify any school-specific edition before publication.
goals: Use divisibility rules to test possible factors.
Express a composite number as a product of primes.
summary: Prime numbers have exactly two positive factors, 1 and themselves. Composite numbers have more than two positive factors. Divisibility, factors, multiples and prime factorisation help explain how whole numbers are built and related.

concepts.title: Factors and multiples
concepts.explanation: A factor divides a number exactly. A multiple is obtained by multiplying a number by a whole number. A number has a finite set of positive factors but infinitely many positive multiples.
concepts.example: Factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. Multiples of 12 include 12, 24, 36 and 48.

concepts.title: Prime numbers
concepts.explanation: A prime number is a whole number greater than 1 with exactly two positive factors: 1 and itself. The number 1 is neither prime nor composite.
concepts.example: 7 is prime because its only positive factors are 1 and 7.

concepts.title: Composite numbers
concepts.explanation: A composite number greater than 1 has more than two positive factors. It can be written as a product of smaller whole numbers greater than 1.
concepts.example: 12 is composite because 12 = 3 × 4 and has more than two factors.

concepts.title: Prime factorisation
concepts.explanation: Prime factorisation writes a composite number as a product of prime numbers. Repeated division or a factor tree can help; stop when every factor is prime.

workedExamples.question: Write 60 as a product of prime factors.

practice.question: Is 1 prime? Explain.
practice.answer: No. It has only one positive factor, while a prime number has exactly two.

practice.question: List the first five positive multiples of 7.
Why is 21 composite?
practice.answer: 21 = 3 × 7, so it has factors other than 1 and itself.
practice.why: A composite number has more than two positive factors.

practice.question: Prime-factorise 24.
practice.why: Keep splitting until every factor is prime.
